sources.entry: Appwrite - End to end backend server for web, native, and mobile developers 🚀. (Source Code) BSD-3-Clause Docker
Appwrite | Backend server for web, mobile and Flutter apps with auth, databases and functions

summary.one_liner: Appwrite is an open-source, self-hostable backend platform for web, mobile, and agent-driven apps, offering auth, databases, storage, functions, messaging, realtime, and hosting.
summary.what_it_does: Appwrite provides a set of backend services exposed through REST, WebSocket/Realtime, GraphQL, and S3-compatible APIs: user authentication (email, SMS, OAuth, anonymous sessions, magic URLs), databases (Appwrite databases or managed PostgreSQL and MySQL), file storage with compression, encryption, and image transformations, and serverless functions running in isolated runtimes. It also includes Sites for deploying static, SSR, and CSR frontends from Git, Messaging for email, SMS, and push, a Firewall for traffic rules and abuse controls, and an MCP server so coding agents can operate on a live project. The README says it can be self-hosted with Docker on any OS that runs the Docker CLI, using a setup wizard on localhost port 20080, or used as Appwrite Cloud. Client SDKs are listed for Web, Flutter, Apple, Android, React Native, and Unity, and server SDKs for Node.js, Python, Dart, PHP, Ruby, .NET, Go, Swift, Kotlin, and Rust.
use_cases: self-host a backend for web or mobile apps
store and transform user uploaded files
run serverless functions with event triggers
connect AI coding agents to a live backend project
deploy frontends from Git with previews
how_to_run: Install Docker on the host machine

Run the installer: docker run -it --rm --publish 127.0.0.1:20080:20080 --volume /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock --volume "$(pwd)"/appwrite:/usr/src/code/appwrite:rw --entrypoint="install" appwrite/appwrite:2.6.2
Open the one-time installer URL printed in the terminal to complete the setup wizard
On Windows, use the CMD or PowerShell variants given in the README
If you hit a Docker API version mismatch, pass --env DOCKER_API_VERSION=<max version>
notable: Hybrid monolithic-microservice architecture with background workers and a message queue
Hosted and local MCP server for coding agents, with OAuth on the hosted version
Setup wizard protected by a one-time installer secret, bound to localhost by default
Managed PostgreSQL and MySQL options alongside Appwrite databases
Client and server SDKs across many languages, generated by a separate SDK Generator project
caveats: Self-hosting requires Docker and a Docker Engine whose API version matches the image; mismatches need a workaround flag
On non-Linux native hosts the server may take a few minutes to start after installation
Appwrite Cloud has a Free plan, with paid plans for scaling
